lesson_title: Racial policy: Nazi treatment of the Jews to 1939
issue: The figure of 'around 400 synagogues' does not appear in any major authoritative source. The USHMM cites either 267 synagogues specifically confirmed burned/destroyed during the two-night pogrom itself, or 'more than 1,400 synagogues' damaged/destroyed across the broader area including Austria and the Sudetenland. The '400' figure is unsupported and falls between both established figures without matching either.
correction: Authoritative sources give two figures: 267 synagogues confirmed burned or destroyed (USHMM specific count for Germany), or more than 1,400 synagogues damaged or destroyed across Germany, Austria and the Sudetenland (USHMM broader count). The lesson should use one of these established figures, e.g. 'more than 1,400 synagogues were attacked or destroyed' or 'around 267 synagogues were burned to the ground'.

claim: On 16 January 1920, Prohibition came into force across the United States.
issue: January 16 is the date the Eighteenth Amendment was ratified (1919), not when Prohibition came into force. Prohibition actually came into force on January 17, 1920, under the terms of the Volstead Act, which set the operative date as one year after ratification (i.e. 17 January 1920). A student writing '16 January 1920' in an exam would be giving a wrong date for when Prohibition started.
correction: Prohibition came into force on 17 January 1920. The Eighteenth Amendment was ratified on 16 January 1919; the Volstead Act set the enforcement start date one year later, at midnight beginning 17 January 1920.

claim: The cost of a Model T fell from $825 in 1908 to $260 by 1925
issue: The 1908 price of the Model T is given as $825 but the established historical figure is $850. Multiple sources including Britannica, Ford Motor Company records and the Library of Congress give the 1908 launch price as $850. The $260 figure for 1925 is correct.
correction: The Model T cost $850 in 1908 (not $825), falling to $260 by 1925.
